title: Online shopping trust, perceived safety, and familiar interface
statement:
In online shopping, trust is supported by perceived safety mechanisms, a familiar interface, and ease of use, so checkout designs can use either a conventional interaction pattern or stronger explanatory trust cues while keeping the transaction flow familiar. (DOI)

Options:
- Familiar checkout: conventional-checkout-pattern (fits: mainstream, low friction, general)
- Security explanation: visible-security-mechanism-copy (fits: risk sensitive, high value, new customer)
- Familiar controls: standardized-form-controls (fits: conventional, accessible, utility first)
- Simple flow: minimal-step-checkout (fits: mobile first, fast, low complexity)
- Payment trust details: trust-details-near-payment (fits: financial risk, high consideration, new customer)
appliesWhen: Applies to: ecommerce, online retail, marketplaces, subscription checkout. Audience: adults, general.

source.title: Trust and TAM in Online Shopping: An Integrated Model
source.authors: David Gefen; Elena Karahanna; Detmar W. Straub
